messages:
Alex Kim: heads-up — noticed a regression on canary after the kernel-selector tweak. short requests (<=64 tokens) are getting queued behind long runs and often time out. looks like batch formation is favoring long sequences more aggressively now, and token budget draining is skews per-tenant fairness. logs attached below.

Maya Patel: ugh. can you paste a short repro / sample traces? is this only after the selector change or also kv/cache config? @Samir any ideas? :thinking_face:

Alex Kim: minimal repro — drive 1k short requests concurrent + a handful of 8k-token requests. short tail p99 jumps to ~2.5s from 300ms on canary. snippet from queue profiler: 

```
queue_depth_by_lane: {short: 8, long: 23}
avg_tokens_per_batch: 1024
token_credits_reserve: {tenant-A: 40, tenant-B: 5}
batch_ejection_count: 12
kv_hit_rate_over_time: tenant-B: 0.62 -> 0.19 after long job
```

Alex Kim: hypothesis: kernel selection prefers a single kernel for long seqs that increases per-batch token capacity which absorbs batching slots and exhausts token credits; meanwhile KV eviction from large contexts causes cache misses for short seqs so KV misses + larger kernel overhead = head-of-line starvation.

Samir Rao: I ran a quick profile (GPU timelines + batcher traces). attaching flame snippet — long sequences hold the compute streams ~3x longer per token due to chosen attention kernel when seq_len > 2048. that increases effective slot occupancy even if token throughput looks ok.

Linda Ho: re: KV — current LRU eviction is size-only. when a big long-run walks through, it populates/refreshes huge context keys and pushes short-req keys out. we should consider tenant-aware KV weights or "short-preserve" TTLs: keep recent <128-token entries pinned for N seconds.

Maya Patel: proposed quick mitigations: 1) add per-tenant min_token_credit (so small tenants can't be drained), 2) preemptive batch ejection threshold: if a queued short request waits > X ms, evict the tail of the oldest long batch to free a slot, 3) KV pinning for entries under a token size. thoughts?

Kevin Zhao: +1. here's a canary config I'd run: 

```yaml
batcher:
  min_tenant_credits: 50 # tokens
  preemptive_eject_ms: 120
  preemptive_token_threshold: 256
kv_cache:
  pin_small_entries: true
  small_entry_ttl_s: 30
  tenant_reserve_ratio: 0.15
kernel_selector:
  long_seq_bias_penalty: 0.8 # lower weight for long-only kernels
```

Kevin Zhao: I'll push this to canary queue on infra-3 for A/B. infra-bot?

infra-bot: scheduled canary deployment: job_id=ci-canary/4821, nodes=infra-3,[g5x2,g5x1], start=2003456900. link: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/4821

deploy-bot: deploy queued (canary). diff: runtime/batcher: add min_tenant_credits + preemptive ejection; runtime/kv: small-entry pin TTL; runtime/kernel: add selection penalty heuristics. change id: d9f3a1c

Maya Patel: instrumentation checklist for the run: capture per-tenant token_credit_time_series, batch_size_distribution, queue_wait_histogram (by seq length), kv_hit_rate_by_tenant, kernel_choice_counts, and tail latency by seq bucket. Also compute "starvation_ratio" = (#short_reqs_waited>preemptive_eject_ms) / total_short_reqs.

Samir Rao: I'll hook up perf harness to synthetic mix (80% short, 20% long) and capture GPU stream traces and NVTX events. expect to look at occupancy and stream idle times.

Linda Ho: if pinning helps KV-hit for short tenants, we should watch memory retention — set tenant_reserve_ratio conservatively. also need fallback plan if canary shows regressions: automatic rollback in 10m window.

Alex Kim: good plan. metrics to watch in the first 30m: p50/p95/p99 short-req latency, starvation_ratio, avg_batch_tokens, kv_hit_rate_short_tenants, overall throughput. if p99 for short goes above 1s or starvation_ratio > 0.05, auto-revert.

Maya Patel: I'll own instrumentation and dashboards. @Kevin please include a canary flag so we can AB (with and without pinning).

Kevin Zhao: will do. running canary now — adding a/b buckets.

infra-bot: canary job started: job_id=ci-canary/4821, start_ts=2003456900

Samir Rao: quick note from first 10m: preemptive_eject_ms=120 reduces average wait for short by ~45%, kv_hit for short tenants improved ~12% with pinning. kernel penalty reduced long-kernel allocation by ~30%. still seeing a few tail cases — investigating.

Alex Kim: nice. can you paste the small trace where a short request still waited >120ms?

Samir Rao: trace => 

```
[2003456923] enqueue short tenant-B (64 tokens) wait start
[2003456923.002] batcher forms batch with two long jobs + 1 short (but short at tail)
[2003456923.140] preemptive check fires, but eject picks a different long batch due to token accounting bug (we removed tenant id from sort key)
[2003456923.270] short finally scheduled -> p99 spike
```

Maya Patel: bug confirmed — preemptive eject comparator still using old sort order, so it sometimes chooses wrong victim. I'll push a fix to include tenant fairness priority in the comparator.

Kevin Zhao: patched comparator and bumped canary job. infra-bot says next run in ~2m.

infra-bot: canary job restarted: job_id=ci-canary/4821, run=2, start_ts=2003457050

Samir Rao: after patch, early signals look clean: short p99 back to ~320ms, starvation_ratio down to 0.8%. KV hit steady. kernel selectors still slightly favor long kernels but penalty is lower.

Linda Ho: recommend we also add a light-weight telemetry counter: "kv_pin_evictions" to watch if pinning causes memory pressure and starts evicting pinned entries.

Alex Kim: agree. let's run this in canary for 2h, collect metrics, and if green, roll to next cluster. thanks all. :thumbsup:
